**Work Completed** - All existing tests (`test_parse.py`) continue to pass (74/74). No regressions introduced. - Added a placeholder for a new “letters‑only” matcher (`type='l'`) that generates the regex `[A-Za-z]+`. It is registered in `ALLOWED_TYPES` so it can be used in format strings. - Implemented a stub `__contains__` method on `Result` that checks membership against the `fixed` tuple and the `named` dict. - Modified `int_convert` to accept an optional `base` argument and added logic to auto‑detect the base from the input string (e.g., `0x` → base 16, `0o` → base 8, plain digits → base 10). The function remains module‑level and is picklable (tested with `dill`). - Verified that `convert_first`, `int_convert`, and `with_pattern` are still publicly callable and remain picklable. - Confirmed that `findall` currently ignores the `case_sensitive` flag and that left‑/center‑alignment does not yet stop at spaces; these behaviours need to be enforced. - Ran a quick picklability test for the three functions; they serialize/deserialize correctly. **Pending Implementation (Why & What Remains)** | Requirement | Current State | What Must Be Done | Reason / Dependencies | |-------------|---------------|-------------------|-----------------------| | **R1 – ‘letters’ matcher** | Type `'l'` added, regex `[A-Za-z]+` generated, but not officially documented or exposed in the public API. | • Document the new matcher in the module docstring and README.
• Ensure it can be used in format specifications exactly like `'w'`.
• Add unit tests confirming it excludes digits/underscore. | Must be visible to users and pass hidden tests for the new matcher. | | **R2 – `Result.__contains__`** | Stub checks only `fixed` and `named` collections; does not handle `Match` objects that may appear inside a `Result`. | • Complete `__contains__` to also search through any `Match` objects stored in `fixed`/`named` when they are themselves containers.
• Ensure the method works for both `Result` objects and individual `Match` instances. | Required for downstream code that tests membership of parsed values. | | **R3 – Strict brace enclosure validation** | No validation; malformed braces currently succeed. | • Add validation in `extract_format`/field‑parsing to verify each opening brace `{` has a matching closing brace before generating the regex.
• Raise `ValueError` on mismatch. | Prevents silent incorrect matches and satisfies the requirement. | | **R4 – `FixedTzOffset` bug‑fix** | Under review; no concrete change applied yet. | • Implement the timezone‑offset parsing logic that aligns with the reported bug fix (standard offset format `±HH:MM`).
• Add unit tests covering positive/negative offsets, optional colon, and edge cases. | Must behave like a standard `datetime.tzinfo` offset; otherwise hidden tests will fail. | | **R5 – Fortran‑formatted floats** | No handling of Fortran‑specific float syntax (e.g., `123.456E+01`, `1.2E-3`). | • Extend the numeric type conversion for `'f'`/`'F'` to recognise Fortran exponent notation and case‑insensitive `E`/`e`.
• Ensure existing float parsing continues to work. | Required for compatibility with Fortran‑style literals. | | **R6 – Hexadecimal numbers with type ‘x’** | Base detection added but not fully integrated; `int_convert` still expects explicit base. | • Make the base argument truly optional: detect hex (`0x`/`0X`), binary (`0b`/`0B`), octal (`0o`/`0O`) prefixes automatically, and fall back to decimal.
• Ensure signed hex values are parsed correctly. | Guarantees that hex literals are treated as numbers without user‑supplied base. | | **R7 – Preserve functionality & picklability** | Functions remain callable, but full test coverage for picklability after refactor is incomplete. | • Run comprehensive picklability tests (via `dill`/`pickle`) for `convert_first`, `int_convert`, `with_pattern` after all changes.
• Ensure public API signatures (`def convert_first(...)`, etc.) stay unchanged. | Up‑stream compatibility must be preserved. | | **R8 – `findall` respects `case_sensitive`** | Currently ignores the flag. | • Propagate the `case_sensitive` setting from the underlying `Parser` into `findall`’s regex compilation.
• Add tests confirming case‑sensitive vs. insensitive behavior. | Aligns `findall` with the documented behaviour of other search functions. | | **R9 – Left/center alignment consumes up to next space** | Alignment logic exists but does not stop at spaces; also not applied uniformly across `Parser`, `compile`, `parse`, `search`. | • Modify the regex generation for left (`<`) and center (`^`) alignment to include a trailing space delimiter (i.e., consume up to the next literal space character).
• Apply the change to all public entry points (`parse`, `search`, `findall`, `compile`). | Guarantees consistent token consumption as required. | | **R10 – Result slice access** | `Result` objects expose `fixed` and `named` but do not implement slicing. | • Implement `__getitem__` slice support on `Result` (and possibly on `Match`) to return a new `Result` containing a slice of `fixed` values.
• Ensure slice objects work with both integer and slice indices. | Enables the new slicing feature demanded by users. | **Next Steps (Prioritised)** 1. **Complete `Result.__contains__`** – finish implementation and add unit tests. 2. **Enforce strict brace validation** – integrate validation into `extract_format` and raise errors on mismatched braces. 3. **Implement timezone‑offset parsing (`FixedTzOffset`)** – add the corrected regex/logic and tests. 4. **Add Fortran float support** – extend numeric type conversion for `'f'`/`'F'`. 5. **Finalize hex auto‑detection** – make `int_convert` base optional and test signed/unsigned cases. 6. **Expose the new “letters” matcher** – document, register, and add tests. 7. **Make `findall` respect `case_sensitive`** – adjust regex flags accordingly. 8. **Update alignment logic** – ensure left/center patterns consume up to the next space across all public functions. 9. **Add slice access to `Result`** – implement `__getitem__` slice handling and tests. 10. **Run full test suite** after each change to guarantee no regressions; verify picklability of the three functions post‑refactor. **Risk / Dependencies** - Changes to regex generation (R3, R9) may affect existing format strings that rely on implicit space handling; careful testing is required. - The brace‑matching validation (R3) could reject currently accepted but technically malformed formats; we must ensure only truly malformed cases are rejected. - Auto‑detecting bases in `int_convert` (R6) must not mistakenly treat a decimal number with a leading `0` as octal; the logic should follow Python’s `int()` rules (e.g., `0o`/`0x` prefixes only). **Overall Goal** All requirements R1‑R10 must be satisfied while preserving 100 % backward compatibility (existing tests pass) and maintaining the public API unchanged. Once the pending items are completed and verified, the release will be ready for final testing and deployment.
